name: Entity Curation
status: reference only -- run when discovery surfaces a batch, never scheduled
description: Turns discovered domains into real companies. Discovery names an entry after its domain ('Acmecorp' for acmecorp.com); curation replaces that with the company's real name, folds a second domain of a known company into its Aliases, files a subsidiary as an Affiliate of its parent, and classifies each -- then the operator flips Ignore to No and the Metadata pipeline builds the hubs.

steps.name: Merge second domains
steps.description: A subdomain or regional domain of a company that already has an entry goes into that entry's Aliases -- not a new company.

steps.name: Research each entity
steps.description: Look the company up online: its real name, what it does, who owns it. Ownership decides the classification.

steps.name: Classify
steps.description: Customer if owned by the local government or a government entity; Partner otherwise, suppliers included. A subsidiary is an Affiliate of its parent, with its own hub.

steps.name: Hold what research cannot settle
steps.description: Left Ignore: Yes with the reason, for the operator -- who knows the correspondence -- to decide.

steps.name: Flip and build
steps.description: Ignore: No on the settled ones; the 30-minute hub job creates them.

notes: An ALIAS says 'same company, second domain'. An AFFILIATE is its own entity with its own hub, People and history. A product of a company is an alias, not a company.
Research changes answers a guess would get wrong: a domain can belong to a company since merged into the operator's own.
Verify after every rewrite that no field on an already-created entry changed. There is no backup of Entities.md.
